title: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Core Principles & Pesticide Safety Manual
source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM), New Delhi
content: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) is the coordinated use of pest and environmental information with available pest control methods to prevent unacceptable levels of pest damage by the most economical means and with the least possible hazard to people, property, and the environment. Hierarchy of IPM controls: 1. Cultural controls (crop rotation, summer deep plowing to expose pupae to birds and solar heat, intercropping, trap crops like marigold in tomato), 2. Mechanical controls (hand picking of egg masses/gregarious larvae, light traps @ 1/ha, yellow/blue sticky cards @ 10-15/acre), 3. Biological controls (conservation of natural enemies like spiders, ladybird beetles, Chrysoperla, Trichogramma), 4. Chemical controls: STRICTLY as last resort and only when pest crosses Economic Threshold Level (ETL). Pesticide safety & legal regulations: Under the Insecticides Act 1968, only Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIBRC) approved pesticides may be used on labeled crops. Banned chemicals (e.g., Endosulfan, Monocrotophos on vegetables, Phorate, Paraquat) MUST NEVER be recommended. Always observe Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI / waiting period) to ensure pesticide residues on harvest remain below Maximum Residue Limits (MRL). Always advise consulting the nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for laboratory pest confirmation.
